questions.stem: In brief: A plaintiff claiming negligence relies on an inference. The fact is within one party's knowledge. Which of the following best describes the legal standard a court would apply?

options.text: A presumption can never be rebutted once its basic fact is shown given the events just recounted.
options.misconception: assumes a presumption is conclusive

options.text: A presumption and an inference are identical in every respect given the events just recounted.
options.misconception: treats a presumption as an inference only

options.text: The presumed fact is the one that must be proved to trigger the presumption given the events just recounted.
options.misconception: confuses the basic and presumed facts

options.text: A presumption requires the factfinder to assume a fact once a basic fact is proved, unless the opposing party produces evidence to rebut it, and its effect on the burden varies by jurisdiction given the events just recounted.

questions.explanation: Presumptions are procedural tools that channel factfinding. Some shift only the burden of producing evidence, while others shift persuasion, so the practical effect depends on the rule creating the presumption. The doctrine controlling this question is presumptions and their effect. The governing statement is: A presumption requires the factfinder to assume a fact once a basic fact is proved, unless the opposing party produces evidence to rebut it, and its effect on the burden varies by jurisdiction given the events just recounted. Option A ("A presumption can never be rebutted once its basic fact is shown given the events just recounted") is wrong because it assumes a presumption is conclusive. Option B ("A presumption and an inference are identical in every respect given the events just recounted") is wrong because it treats a presumption as an inference only. Option C ("The presumed fact is the one that must be proved to trigger the presumption given the events just recounted") is wrong because it confuses the basic and presumed facts.
questions.hint: Ask what fact triggers the presumption and what the other side must do to meet it. Keep the inquiry on presumptions and their effect.
